vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: soul-in-sapphire
Version: 1.0.4

The skill is classified as suspicious due to critical vulnerabilities that could lead to arbitrary code execution (RCE) and arbitrary file writes. Multiple scripts (e.g., `scripts/ltm_common.js`, `scripts/notionctl_bridge.js`, `scripts/setup_ltm.js`, `scripts/emostate_tick.js`) use `execFileSync` to run an external `notionctl.mjs` script, whose path can be overridden by the `NOTIONCTL_PATH` environment variable. If an attacker controls this environment variable, they can achieve RCE. Additionally, `scripts/state_recall.js` allows writing arbitrary JSON content to a user-specified file path via the `--write` argument, posing an arbitrary file write vulnerability. There is no evidence of intentional malicious behavior such as data exfiltration or backdoor installation.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with its stated Notion-based long‑term memory / emotion / journal purpose: it requires only Node and a Notion token, uses a local config, delegates API calls to a local notionctl helper, and contains scripts to create/query Notion databases and write/read local config/log files.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Notion LTM, emotion/state, journal, subagent spawn planning) matches the code and declared requirements: Node, NOTION_API_KEY, a local config (~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json), and a dependency on a Notion helper skill. Required env/binaries align with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts operate on Notion (pages/databases), the local config in the user's home, and local skill-state files. They do read/write ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json and may read a workspace IDENTITY.md to default the base name — both are consistent with setup needs but do touch local files. Scripts log spawn payloads under skill state directories; this can record task text and payloads (expected for subagent workflow). No instructions attempt to read shell history, other credentials, or exfiltrate data to external endpoints beyond Notion.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-and-script-only package (no install spec). It executes a sibling notionctl script (notion-api-automation) via node child process; no remote downloads or archive extraction occur. That is appropriate for a Notion integration but relies on the presence/trust of the notion-api-automation tool.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only NOTION_API_KEY is required as a credential (declared as primary). An optional NOTIONCTL_PATH allows overriding the notionctl executable. No unrelated credentials or broad environment access are requested. Note: SKILL.md mentions NOTION_TOKEN as alternate, but only NOTION_API_KEY is declared — minor documentation mismatch.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not forced-always; it runs when invoked. It writes a config file under the user's home (~/.config/soul-in-sapphire) and appends logs under local skill state directories — these are normal for persistent LTM tooling. It does not modify other skills' configs or request system-wide privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent with its Notion LTM/journal intent, but review these before installing: 1) You must supply NOTION_API_KEY — that token grants this skill permission to read/write your Notion workspace; prefer a dedicated integration with minimal scopes. 2) The skill will create and manage databases and write a local config at ~/.config/soul-in-sapphire/config.json — the config contains Notion database and data_source IDs; do not commit it to version control. 3) The code calls a local notionctl helper (notion-api-automation). Ensure that dependency is installed from a trusted source because the skill executes it as a child process. 4) Subagent/spawn-related logs and payloads are appended to local state/log files and may contain task text or sensitive content; check the spawn profiles and logs if you care about what's persisted. 5) Optional NOTIONCTL_PATH allows pointing to an alternate executable — only set this to a trusted path. If you want extra assurance, inspect the notion-api-automation scripts and run the setup in a test workspace before giving it access to your primary Notion account.
